changes.balance: The surplus pricing is now a week old and the tape is pausing inside it, while the traded Canadian strip tightens on volume against the December space allocation, which says the basin residual and the market disagree and the market is the one trading.
changes.body: Brent Jan27 settled $91.98, up $0.03, and WTI Dec26 settled $83.21, down $0.05, on Thursday (Reuters, Nov 19), and Asia bid Brent $92.77 and WTI Jan27 $83.15 at 0404 GMT on Friday (Reuters, Nov 20). Both benchmarks are set for a third straight weekly loss, Brent down about 3.5 percent and December WTI down almost 6 percent on the week. December WTI expires today.
changes.conditional: A weekend Hormuz incident that removes a named vessel or a measured flow print below the last gauge reprices the front against the surplus; a quiet weekend leaves the surplus pricing in charge into the Nov 29 OPEC+ meeting.
changes.delta: Thursday settled flat, Brent up three cents and WTI down five cents, Asia bid both benchmarks about 0.9 percent on Friday morning, and both remain set for a third straight weekly loss
changes.title: Thursday settled flat inside the repricing, Asia bid Friday morning, and the week still belongs to the surplus
changes.vintage: Reuters settles, Nov 19, 2026, and overnight tape at 0404 GMT, Nov 20, 2026

changes.balance: The traded strip tightening on volume into a harder December space allocation is the market's verdict on the balance residual: either the production estimates are too high or the egress capacity is too low, and the strip is pricing one of those corrections rather than a storage build.
changes.body: January WCS settled -$22.00 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 19), up $1.45 on 670 lots, with February at -$21.55 on 295 lots and March at -$21.20 on 240 lots, the third straight tightening session on volume. January Houston WCS settled -$14.40 (ICE ARV settle, Nov 19) on 990 lots, which puts the January ARV to TMW spread at +$7.60. December Mainline apportionment is Light 24 percent and Heavy 17 percent at Kerrobert (Enbridge notice, announced Nov 18). WCS is deeply discounted at both locations while the location spread stays orderly and no storage bid is priced, which points to destination market discounting and easing freight transmission rather than a trapped basin.
changes.conditional: A strip that holds its tightening through next week against the December allocation confirms the repricing; a strip that gives the tightening back reopens the widening path for the front.
changes.delta: January WCS tightened $1.45 to -$22.00 on 670 lots, the front month itself trading, with the January export spread at +$7.60, a day after December apportionment printed Light 24 percent and Heavy 17 percent
changes.source: ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 19, 2026; Enbridge apportionment notice, announced Nov 18, 2026
changes.title: The traded strip tightened for a third session on volume, with the front month itself trading

changes.balance: The incident tempo and the flow gauges still point in different directions: total Gulf exports including bypass are near pre-war while the strait itself was last measured at 48 percent of pre-war, and a market settling flat through a strike on Riyadh is pricing the bypass-inclusive gauge.
changes.body: A Houthi strike damaged the PIF Tower in Riyadh's financial district on Thursday, the second strike on the district this month, with no injuries and no Saudi oil supply impact reported. JMIC Update 115 counts seven incidents since its previous update and rates further attacks highly likely in the next 24 to 48 hours. The Tara Gas fire appears under control. Iran's Nov 19 claim of two supertankers hitting mines is unverified with no vessel named. The last measured strait only clearance is 8,264 kb/d to Nov 11, 48 percent of pre-war, now nine days old, while total Gulf exports including bypass routes ran about 16.7 million barrels a day since Oct 1 against about 17 million pre-war.
changes.conditional: A fresh measured strait only print near the last gauge reprices the front against the surplus; a measured print near pre-war levels confirms the incident tempo is noise for deliverable supply.
changes.delta: The PIF Tower in Riyadh was struck on Thursday, further Hormuz attacks are rated highly likely within 24 to 48 hours, and the strait only flow gauge is now nine days old with no fresher measured print
changes.source: Reuters, Nov 19 to 20, 2026; JMIC Update 115, reported Nov 19, 2026; Kpler briefing, Nov 13, 2026
changes.title: Riyadh was struck again, more Hormuz attacks are rated likely within 48 hours, and the flow gauge is nine days old
changes.vintage: Kpler briefing, Nov 13, 2026, data to Nov 11

flags.body: December Mainline apportionment (Light 24 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 17 percent at Kerrobert) is announced for December, up from November's Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent. The Cromer and Superior points for December were not found in any public source. The traded differential strip tightened for a third straight session on volume after the notice, with January WCS settling -$22.00 on 670 lots, and the balance residual is qualified against that pricing rather than carried as a storage forecast.
flags.title: December apportionment: Light 24 and Heavy 17 at Kerrobert, up from 19 and 7 in November
flags.trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment percentages as published in the notice itself

flags.body: JMIC Update 115 counts seven incidents since its previous update and rates further attacks highly likely in the next 24 to 48 hours, with the threat level remaining SEVERE. The PIF Tower in Riyadh was struck on Thursday with no oil supply impact reported. The last measured strait only clearance is 8,264 kb/d to Nov 11, 48 percent of pre-war, and is now nine days old, while total Gulf exports including bypass routes ran about 16.7 million barrels a day since Oct 1 against about 17 million pre-war. A confirmed measured flow print resolves which gauge the pricing should follow.
flags.title: Attacks rated highly likely within 48 hours, and the strait only flow gauge is nine days old
flags.trigger: A fresh measured clearance print from a tracker, or a confirmed loadings halt from an owner or UKMTO product

flags.body: The North Dakota Pipeline chloride disruption ran a sixth day on Thursday, with flows still suppressed as of Thursday morning on an analyst read and a force majeure at MPLX reported alongside the earlier Flint Hills Pine Bend report. Enbridge has not confirmed a shut-in and no restart timeline has been published.
flags.title: North Dakota Pipeline chloride disruption on its sixth day, with no restart timeline
flags.trigger: An Enbridge statement on the disruption, or a reported restart of normal operations
